title: 8 Best AI phone systems for businesses
summary: Overwhelmed by all the AI phone platforms on the market? Compare the eight best AI phone systems for businesses here.
body_markdown:
Somewhere between that last service call and your latest estimate, three new missed calls appeared on your phone. If that sounds familiar, it’s a common issue. In fact,[78% of people abandon businesses after missed calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-callback-statistics/) — and 82% call competitors.


AI phone systems help you avoid missing calls altogether by answering 24/7 or just when your team is busy. They can also help to transcribe conversations, generate summaries, and qualify leads. That way, you’re not leaving money on the table.


We tested several top AI business phone systems and narrowed it down to eight options. These include:


- **Quo** — the best AI phone system for small and growing businesses
- **Dialpad** — the best AI phone system for built-in video meetings
- **RingCentral** — the best AI phone system for desk phone support
- **Nextiva** — the best AI phone system for omnichannel communication
- **Allo** — the best AI phone system for mobile-first small teams


Below, you can compare these platforms and others based on price, reliability, and AI features that matter for daily business use.


##


**Our methodology: How we evaluated the top AI phone systems**


We followed a two-step process to determine the best AI phone systems for small businesses. First, we signed up for free trials, contacted sales and support, and tested each platform’s call reliability firsthand. Then we researched user reviews and publicly available documentation.


Here are the factors we weighed:


1. **Price.** We evaluated the cost of each plan, including hidden fees and which useful AI features are included versus which were add-ons.
2. **AI features.** These include call summaries, transcriptions, and[AI receptionists](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/receptionist) , which we evaluated to see whether they worked well and didn’t feel bolted on.
3. **Core calling features.** This includes the business phone features that should be available on entry-level plans, like call routing and recording.
4. **Support.** We evaluated how quickly and how well each provider’s support team responds, and which channels they use.
5. **Call quality.** We tested the platform’s reliability and uptime firsthand, and assessed it through user reviews.
6. **Scalability.** We checked to see whether plans cap users, minutes, or messages as your team grows.


##


**8 Best AI phone systems for businesses**


Here’s a quick snapshot of how the best AI phone systems compare:


Provider Best for Starting price Key AI features


Quo Small and growing businesses $15 per user per month Sona, Quo Agent, call summaries and transcripts, AI call tags, contact suggestions, Claude and ChatGPT MCP


Dialpad Built-in video meetings $15 per user per month on Connect; $39 per user per month on Sales Real-time AI speech coaching, sentiment analysis, and AI scorecards


Nextiva Omnichannel communication $15 per user per month AI call notes, summaries, an AI receptionist, and NextIQ AI Answer Assist


RingCentral Desk phone support $20 per user per month AI IVR with intelligent call routing, AI Writer with an upgrade, AI assistant for SMS with an upgrade, AI Virtual Assistant with an upgrade, and the AIR Receptionist available as an add-on


Aircall Call centers $30 per user per month AI Assist add-on for call summaries, sentiment analysis, and CRM logging


Grasshopper Phone number extensions $14 per month AI call summaries, AI call and voicemail sentiment analysis, and a Virtual Receptionist, with an add-no


Zoom Phone Existing Zoom Workplace users $10.50 per user per month for metered calling AI Companion for real-time call insights, voicemail summaries, AI notetaking, and access to the AI companion


Allo Mobile-first small teams $10 per user per month, coming soon AI IVR, AI search assistant referencing past calls and texts, and an AI voice agent available as an add-on


### **1. Quo, formerly OpenPhone: Best AI phone system for small and growing businesses**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling and texting in the US and Canada on every plan
- Shared numbers and inboxes
- AI voice agent Sona answers calls 24/7
- On-demand and automatic call recording options
- AI call summaries, transcripts, and call tags
- Native and third-party integrations
- Connectors with Claude and ChatGPT along with the Quo MCP
- Support for desktop, browser, and mobile apps


#### Cons


- Can’t verify accounts through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. For safety reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a business phone system built for small and growing service businesses. It lets you work together as a team from a shared inbox and scale your reach with AI without losing the personal touch.


Every Quo plan comes with unlimited calling and texting in the US and Canada, plus one local US, Canadian, or North American toll-free number per user.


You’ll also have access to[Sona](http://quo.com/sona) , Quo’s[AI voice agent](http://quo.com/product/ai/voice-agent) . It can pick up the phone 24/7 for your team or just when your team is busy. This prevents callers from giving up and going to competitors. It also keeps track of callers automatically so your team can follow up later.


Sona can even[capture leads via text](https://www.quo.com/sona#:~:text=Capture%20leads%20over%20SMS) by answering questions and collecting their information. You can even set up conditional routing so Sona only takes calls from non-saved contacts. That way, Sona filters out spam and can qualify leads.


Every Sona call results in a summary and transcript. You can also set up automatic call recording, transcripts, and summaries for any calls your team handles. This means your team won’t have to worry about manual notetaking after every call. You can also get visibility into every conversation. On the Scale plan, you also get AI call tags. These automatically organize calls by the tags you set, like customer sentiment or competitor keywords. Then you can spot calls that need attention without sorting through them yourself.


You can also get answers about any conversation or customer using[Quo Agent](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/quo-agent) , which is available on any plan. For example, you might ask: “Who should I follow up with?” or “Give me a summary of what’s been said to John Doe.” Plus, you can easily look for patterns in your analytics. Try asking: “How many calls did we miss last week?” or “How many follow-ups have been done this month?”


Want to automate additional tasks? Connect Quo to AI tools like[Claude](https://www.quo.com/blog/claude-integration/) and ChatGPT. For example, you might ask ChatGPT to spot patterns in your call logs and find places to optimize your process. Or you might use Claude to schedule recurring tasks, like creating and sending out daily call reports.


Chase Gallagher at[CMG Landscaping](https://www.quo.com/customers/cmg-landscaping) was a client who[connected Quo to ChatGPT](https://www.quo.com/integrations/chatgpt) to ask questions fast. That way, he can ask who handled calls best that week or how many follow-ups a rep made. “I can go through the information I need to see a lot quicker than if I’m just sitting here reading,” he says.


Using Quo and Sona together has helped CMG Landscaping:


- Reduce missed calls from 43% to 7%
- Save 40 to 60 hours per month onboarding new hires
- Avoid $70,000 per year in unnecessary HR costs
- Turn quotes around in 24 to 48 hours


See why 90,000+ businesses trust Quo by[signing up for a seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) . During the trial, test Sona with your team and take the first 10 calls free.


#### **Quo pricing**


Quo has three pricing tiers:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls and texts, shared numbers, AI contact suggestions, Zapier integration, and more
- **Business:** $23 per user per month to access phone menus with IVR,[call transfers](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding/call-transfer) , analytics, CRM integrations,[Claude](https://www.quo.com/integrations/claude) and[ChatGPT](https://www.quo.com/integrations/chatgpt) connectors, 10 free calls per month with our AI voice agent, Sona, and more
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for AI call tags, dedicated onboarding, inbound phone support, and priority chat and email support


For more than 10 calls a month, you can purchase additional Sona credits. These are more predictable than per-minute pricing, which can easily spike your bill when customers need more help over the phone.


Here’s what to expect from Sona’s bundled pricing:


Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5


Sona tiers Free $25 per month $49 per month $99 per month $199 per month


Included credits 1,000 credits/10 calls 4,000 credits/40 calls 10,000 credits/100 calls 25,000 credits/250 calls 60,000 credits/600 calls


Overage rate per call $1.00 $0.75 $0.65 $0.55 $0.45


### **2. Dialpad: Best for teams that want video meetings built in**


#### Pros


- Live call transcription and real-time analytics
- Real-time AI-powered speech coaching
- Local number support in 50+ countries


#### Cons


- Outbound texting capped at 250 messages per user per month before overage charges
- Additional phone numbers require a tier upgrade
- Reported SMS setup delays per Trustpilot reviews


Dialpad is a[cloud phone system](http://quo.com/blog/best-cloud-phone-system) for teams that want video meetings built into their phone system. It offers three main products: Connect, Sales, and Support. Connect, its phone system for small businesses, comes with minimal AI features. This includes real-time transcriptions and automated call summaries.


Switch to a Sales or Support product to access tools like AI-driven sentiment analysis. This feature flags a shift in customer sentiment during a call and notifies supervisors so they can jump in before it escalates.


You can also purchase Dialpad add-ons that unlock more AI features, such as its AI Agent. Other add-ons include AI CSAT, AI scorecards, and AI live coaching calls. Keep in mind these require a more expensive Sales or Support plan and aren’t available on the Connect plan at all.


Dialpad also comes with texting limitations. There’s an SMS cap of 250 messages on every Connect plan. If you go over the limit, expect to see an increase in your monthly bill. And if you’re on a Sales or Support plan, you’ll pay $0.008 per inbound and outbound text for each message.


Many past users also report that texting is hard to set up with Dialpad. Others say it can be somewhat unreliable. None of this is ideal for growing teams that rely on texting.


If you’re looking for an AI phone system that lets you call *and* text without limits, you may want to investigate a[Dialpad alternative](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) .


#### Dialpad pricing


**


[Dialpad’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) includes three main products: Connect, Sales, and Support.


Here’s what you can expect to pay for Dialpad Connect:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calling,[multi-level IVR](https://www.quo.com/blog/multi-level-ivr/) , toll-free number support, call recording, and voicemail greetings
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month for international texting support, additional numbers, third-party integrations, and 25 ring groups
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for unlimited ring groups, additional integrations, and a 100% uptime guarantee


Dialpad’s best AI features are available as add-ons on the Sales and Support products.


Here’s what you’ll pay for a Sales plan:


- **Essentials:** $39 per user per month for call recording and transcription, coaching team setup, call monitoring with whisper and barge, and AI Recaps that sync to your CRM
- **Advanced:** $95 per user per month for local presence dialing, real-time objection guidance, CRM moment logging, and voicemail drop
- **Premium:** $150 per user per month for AI Playbooks, AI Scorecards, and inbound call queuing and routing


And here’s what you’ll pay for a Support plan:


- **Essentials:** $80 per user per month for call routing and queuing, real-time agent status monitoring, and call transcription and recording
- **Advanced:** $115 per user per month for live agent coaching cards, CRM moment logging, and additional channel support
- **Premium:** $150 per user per month for automated quality management, AI CSAT scoring on all calls, advanced analytics, and workforce management included as an add-on


Dialpad’s AI agent can help customers with scheduling, routing, order lookups, and more. Pricing requires a custom quote. The site *does* mention you’ll need to purchase AI agent Credits to use it.


### **3. Nextiva: Best for omnichannel communication**


#### Pros


- Desktop and mobile apps
- AI transcription and call summaries are available
- Routes voice, chat, SMS, and social channels like WhatsApp into one inbox


#### Cons


- AI features are reserved for higher tiers
- Toll-free numbers and minutes require an upgrade
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- SMS is capped at 100 messages per user per month on the base plan


Nextiva is a unified communications system for customer conversations beyond calls and texts. You can manage conversations across website chat, review sites, and social messaging apps like WhatsApp. It even supports video meetings, with an add-on for a Microsoft Teams integration.


Nextiva offers AI features like transcriptions and call summaries. Just keep in mind these require multiple upgrades. Nextiva also offers XBert, itsAI receptionist. This is available as an add-on for all plans, but there’s no free trial.


Nextiva’s base plan also has many other limitations. For example, you only get 100 SMS messages per user per month. Even toll-free numbers and minutes require an upgrade.


Nextiva is a solid AI phone system for teams that rely on other digital communication channels. But if you’re a small and growing team, you might end up paying for more than you need for features that are standard on[Nextiva alternatives](http://quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives) .


#### Nextiva pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Nextiva’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls and video meetings, auto-attendant and call menus, voicemail transcription, team messaging, and 100 text messages
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for 2,000 free toll-free minutes, smart call routing as an add-on, add-ons with CRM integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot, and 500 text messages
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for 10,000 free toll-free minutes, real-time transcription, AI call notes and summaries, NextIQ AI Answer Assist, drag-and-drop workflow builder, full conversation history across channels, and unlimited text messages


Nextiva’s XBert AI receptionist starts at $99 per month. That includes 100 resolutions across calls, texts, and chats. There’s a $0.99 overage fee for each additional resolution.


### **4. RingCentral: Best for desk phone support**


#### Pros


- Desk phone support on every plan
- Toll-free number support
- UCaaS tools, including video conferencing and webinars
- AI Receptionist is available


#### Cons


- 25 SMS messages per user per month on the base plan
- Call recordings are deleted after 90 days
- Caps on toll-free minutes
- Per-minute pricing makes budgeting unpredictable


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) is a UCaaS platform that offers desk phones, video conferencing, calling, and texting. Every plan includes AI features for calls, videos, and team chat. For example, you can summarize unread team messages, transcribe calls, and take real-time notes. Upgrade your plan to unlock the AI assistant for SMS, which can help write and edit texts. It can also translate texts so your team can provide multilingual support.


An[AI answering service](https://www.quo.com/answering-service) called AIR is available, but RingCentral charges per-minute pricing. Prices start at $39 per month with the RingEX Core plan. You get 100 minutes included, which are rounded up and billed in 30-second increments. If you exceed that number, you’ll pay $0.50 per minute. This could make your budgeting unpredictable. For example, if a scheduling issue keeps customers on calls longer than usual, you might see an unexpected bump in your monthly bill.


As one user wrote:


*“A one-second AI receptionist pickup is considered a full minute. They also got rid of my robocall blocking feature, and I started getting robocalls again. I knew it was deliberate because they knew it would eat up my AI receptionist minutes so they could charge more.”* —[Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a469892afd8a1b778250b37)


Apart from[RingCentral AI](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-ai/) , other drawbacks include few toll-free minutes, SMS, and file storage limits. On the base plan, you only get 25 texts per user per month, 100 toll-free minutes, and limited storage. You do get “unlimited” storage if you upgrade, but recordings are deleted after 90 days.


#### RingCentral pricing


**


This is[RingCentral pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) for the AI phone system product:


- **Core:** $20 per user per month for unlimited domestic calls, on-demand call recording, 25 texts, 100 pooled toll-free minutes, AI IVR with intelligent call routing, and the AI Receptionist available as an add-on, starting at $39 per month
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month for CRM integrations, 100 texts, 1,000 pooled toll-free minutes, multi-site support, and access to the AI Writer
- **Ultra:** $35 per user per month for 200 texts, 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, RingCentral Webinar, historical and real-time analytics, “unlimited” storage, the AI assistant for SMS, and all AI Virtual Assistant features
- **Customer Engagement Bundle:** Contact for pricing for a shared SMS inbox, company reply templates, SMS compliance management, queue callback, wait time and place alerts, and live reports


RingCentral’s AIR receptionist starts at $39 per month, as long as you tack it onto a phone plan. If you want to use the AIR *outside* of RingCentral, pricing starts at $49 per month.


### **5. Aircall: Best for call centers**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada
- Advanced analytics and performance dashboards


#### Cons


- Most AI features are add-ons
- Minimum seat requirement drives up costs
- Voice agent is on per-minute pricing
- Reported billing and cancellation friction, according to user reviews


[Aircall](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-alternatives/) is a call center phone system built for sales and support teams. In addition to unlimited calls in the US and Canada, you also get analytics and performance dashboards for each team member. This can help you track performance and spot bottlenecks that could affect closing rates or CSAT scores.


You get a few AI features on every plan, like call and voicemail transcriptions. There’s also a filterable log of calls and voicemails, which Aircall dubs its AI “Conversation Center.” Beyond that, there are no AI features on other plans. Instead, you’ll need to purchase an add-on for specific features, like AI call summaries or CRM logging.


Just keep in mind that all Aircall plans have user minimums, which increase the cost alongside the AI add-on prices. The base plan, for instance, has a three-user minimum. This means you’ll pay at least $90 per month, plus $27 for AI Assist or $147 for AI Assist Pro.


#### Aircall pricing


**


[Aircall’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing/) has three tiers:


- **Essentials:** $30 per user per month for unlimited inbound and domestic outbound calls, one local or toll-free number, call transcriptions, and call recording for up to one year, with a three-user minimum
- **Professional:** $50 per user per month for unlimited call recording, advanced analytics, call whispering, voicemail drop, and access to the PowerDialer, with a three-user minimum
- **Custom:** Contact for pricing for unlimited international calling, an included Analytics+ add-on, premium onboarding, and prioritized support, with a 25-user minimum


Here’s what you’ll pay for Aircall’s AI add-ons:


- **AI Assist:** $9 per user per month for call summaries, topic recognition, talk-to-listen ratios, action items, sentiment analysis, trending topics, call scoring, CRM logging, automated email follow-ups, and access to Aircall’s AI and transcription API
- **AI Assist Pro:** $49 per user per month for custom call summaries, standard and custom playbooks, live transcription, playbook CRM logging, live prompting, contact insights, and automated call scoring with custom questions
- **AI Voice Agents:** $175 for 500 minutes, or pay-as-you-go for $0.49 per minute for up to 2,500 minutes, CRM logging, warm transfers to humans, FAQs, and appointment scheduling


### **6. Grasshopper: Best for phone number extensions**


#### Pros


- Multi-digit phone number extensions
- Unlimited users on higher tiers
- Simple setup for solo operators


#### Cons


- Limited integrations
- Limited productivity features
- Call recording requires an upgrade


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) is a virtual phone system built for solo operators and very small teams. It offers multi-digit extensions on upgraded plans. This can help you create separate lines for people or departments on the same phone number.


[Grasshopper’s AI features](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-ai/) are new as of 2026. So far, they include:


- AI voicemail sentiment
- AI call sentiment, which requires an upgrade
- Call summaries, which require an upgrade


Grasshopper also offers an integration with Smith.ai’s AI receptionist. This lets you forward calls to Smith.ai’s platform from one of your Grasshopper extensions.


Just keep in mind this logs your calls *outside* of Grasshopper, so you’ll need to tab between both tools to get the full context of conversations. You’ll also need a separate[Smith.ai plan](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-pricing) , starting at $150 per month.


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Grasshopper’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) :


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one user, one business phone number, one extension, unlimited calling and texting, mobile and desktop apps, call forwarding, custom greetings, voicemail with transcription, instant response, virtual fax, and AI voicemail sentiment
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for unlimited users, one business phone number, three extensions, call recording, IVR, call summaries, simultaneous call handling, and AI call sentiment
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for unlimited users, four business phone numbers, unlimited extensions, and everything in Solo Plus


### **7. Zoom Phone: Best for existing Zoom Workplace users**


#### Pros


- Natively connected to Zoom Workplace video meetings
- Call recording is included on every plan
- Standalone AI receptionist is available
- Bundled discount pricing is available when paired with Zoom Workplace


#### Cons


- Unlimited domestic calling requires an upgrade from the base metered plan
- Shared numbers are capped at 10 teammates with four concurrent calls
- Third-party phone integrations are limited compared to more robust business phone systems


Zoom Phone is the calling companion to Zoom’s video platform. If your team already uses Zoom Workplace, you can use Zoom Phone to make calls and send texts in addition to video calling.Every Zoom Phone plan offers basic AI features. For example, you get AI notetaking on three calls per month. If you upgrade your plan, you can access an agent builder, custom meeting summary templates, and unlimited AI notetaking.


Want more AI features? You’ll need Zoom’s AI Companion. This can help you summarize SMS threads, get real-time AI insights during calls, and create to-dos from voicemails. But this is only available on the Customer Engagement Pack add-on.


Where Zoom Phone falls short is with its base plan, which forces you to upgrade if you want unlimited domestic calling. You’ll also need to upgrade several times to access CRM integrations. Even then, some past users say these integrations feel shallow compared to other[Zoom Phone alternatives](http://quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-alternatives) . That’s because it’s primarily designed for its own infrastructure, not third-party tools.


See for yourself:


*“Another area for improvement is that Zoom Phone works best when the organization is already committed to the Zoom ecosystem. If a team uses different tools for meetings, messaging, CRM, support, or contact center workflows, the overall value may depend on how well Zoom Phone integrates into those existing processes.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-zoom-phone/reviews/zoom-phone-review-12762957)


#### Zoom Phone pricing


**


Zoom Phone’s pricing depends on the number of minutes and AI features you want. Plans include:


- **US & Canada Metered:** $10.50 per user per month for metered domestic calling, unlimited domestic SMS and MMS, 50 pages of online fax, and AI features like AI call summaries, voicemail prioritization, and AI Companion
- **US & Canada Unlimited:** $16 per user per month for all Metered features, plus unlimited domestic calling
- **Pro Plus:** $20.50 per user per month for video management tools, Workplace integrations like Microsoft and Salesforce, 15 GB cloud storage per user, unlimited AI meeting summaries, access to the agent builder, and eight custom AI meeting summary templates


- **Global Select:** $22 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling in 40+ countries and territories, one direct dial number per license, and unlimited online fax
- **Business Plus:** $24.50 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, 300 meeting participants, device management, 15 GB cloud storage per user, unlimited AI notetaking, summaries, and queries


There’s also a standalone AI receptionist add-on starting at $25 per month for 100 minutes per month.


### **8. Allo: Best for mobile-first small teams**


#### Pros


- Cost-effective Solo plan for single users is coming soon
- AI IVR and an AI assistant that references past calls and texts as a knowledge base
- Supports 20+ countries and multiple languages


#### Cons


- Pricing jumps dramatically between plans
- Base plan doesn’t support sending texts or the desktop app
- Base plan only stores AI summaries and transcripts for 30 days


Allo is a newer phone system built for sales teams. Its current base plan for teams, Business, starts at $32 per month for calling, texting, and team messaging. This includes AI features for its IVR, plus an AI search assistant to find details about contacts or conversations. You’ll unlock its AI voice agent for $32 extra per month.


A more affordable plan is in the works for single users only. But in return for $120 per year, you’ll lose access to outbound texting and the desktop app. You’ll still have access to AI summaries and transcripts, but they’re only stored for 30 days. If you want more AI *and* more storage space, you’ll need Allo’s Business plan.


Another thing to know about Allo: past users say it’s not feature-rich yet. Since it’s a newer tool, it’s missing tools and offering services that aren’t as advanced as other competitors.


This reviewer provides some firsthand knowledge:


*“Yes, there are certain features that could be improved, like the dashboard. Some missing features, especially on the standard plan, are still inferior to what we currently have on Onoff Business, so that’s quite unfortunate.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/the-mobile-first-company-allo/reviews/allo-review-12314842)


#### Allo pricing


**


Allo has three pricing plans to choose from:


- **Solo:** $120 per year for one user, unlimited national calls, one number, call recording, AI call summaries and transcripts, and email support. At the time of writing, this plan isn’t publicly available yet.
- **Business:** $32 per user per month for unlimited users with one number each, CRM sync with call tags in[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) ,[Pipedrive](https://www.quo.com/integrations/pipedrive) ,[Attio](https://www.quo.com/integrations/attio) , and[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce) , SMS support, custom AI summary templates, AI post-call actions, call analytics, and MCP connectors with Claude and ChatGPT
- **Ultra:** $100 per user per month for AI agents like the AI SDR, AI CRM manager, and AI sales coach, custom analytics dashboards, a custom AI voice for IVR, Slack support, a dedicated account manager, and custom onboarding


The AI receptionist costs $32 per agent per month, or the price of a Business user seat, to answer inbound calls.


##


**How to choose the right AI phone system**


There are a lot of options for AI phone systems. Each one is best for specific use cases. Use the steps below to pick the right platform for you:


- **Team size and growth.** Check what plan minimums and per-seat pricing look like at your current headcount, not just the number on the pricing page. Some providers require a minimum seat count to unlock a plan, which can inflate costs for small teams.
- **The AI features you need on the base plan.** Some providers build core AI capabilities into every plan, while others charge separately for features like call transcripts. Check which model a provider uses before comparing sticker prices. The same $20 per month plan can end up costing three times that once you add the AI features you need.
- **Price scalability as you grow.** Does the phone system provider match their offering to your business size? For example, charging by conversation with your voice agent means you only pay for what you need. But if you’re charged by the minute, you may end up paying more during busy seasons or long conversations — which can get pricey fast.
- **Connections with third-party tools.** Check whether the AI phone system integrates with other AI tools you already rely on, like Claude or ChatGPT, not just CRMs. Also compare how many native Zapier or Make integrations each provider offers versus what you’d have to build yourself through their API.


##


**Set up Quo, the best AI phone system, today**


The “right” AI phone system for your business depends on where your team needs the most support. Whether that’s missed calls, manual notetaking, or missing context for teams, an AI-first phone system like Quo is the best place to start.


Every plan includes Sona, Quo’s AI voice agent, that can handle calls 24/7. You also get Quo Agent, which answers questions about your data and performs tasks like updating contacts and creating follow-up tasks you can assign to your team. Upgrade to the Business plan for call summaries and transcripts of every call, plus CRM integrations with the tools you already use. Upgrade to the Scale plan to add AI call tags in addition to everything above.


Sign up today for[Quo’s seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup?ps_partner_key=YzZiZGQ5ZTBlMDcy&ps_xid=Ce0lhPvdNIWECO) and confirm our AI phone system is right for your needs.


##


**FAQs**


****What is an AI phone system?****


An AI phone system is any business phone platform with built-in artificial intelligence. Beyond making and receiving calls, you can use AI to:
– Transcribe conversations and generate call summaries
– Tag calls by topic or sentiment
– Automatically qualify leads
– Answer calls 24/7 through an AI voice agent


****What are the best AI automated phone systems for businesses?****


The “best” AI automated phone system depends on your business needs. For example, most small and growing businesses rely on Quo for voice AI agents, AI call tags, and connectors with Claude and ChatGPT. If you need features like video, consider a unified communications platform like RingCentral. Larger brands might do better with enterprise-friendly platforms like Nextiva.


****How do you set up a business phone system?****


Using Quo as an example, here’s how to set up a business VoIP phone system in five steps:

****What is an AI answering service?****


An AI answering service is a tool that can answer incoming calls without a human receptionist. Some, like Smith.ai, are standalone tools, so you need a separate phone system to forward calls from. Others, like Sona, are built into your business phone system.


****How does a cloud phone system work?****


A cloud phone system sends calls and texts over the internet instead of traditional phone wires. First, download an app on your phone, computer, or tablet. Then connect to the internet to make or receive calls from your business number. Everything runs 100% in the cloud, so you can add users, change numbers, and update call flows from anywhere with an internet connection.


****Do AI answering services integrate with CRMs?****


Most modern AI phone systems integrate with popular CRMs like HubSpot, Salesforce, and Pipedrive. Some of these integrations are native, meaning you can easily set them up in a few clicks. Others require a third-party connection through tools like Zapier or Make.


****Should you choose a standalone AI answering service or an AI-enabled phone system?****


The “best” choice between a standalone AI service and an AI-enabled phone system depends on your business needs. A standalone system requires an extra tool to manage and comes with a separate bill. In contrast, an AI-enabled phone system integrates an AI voice agent into your existing phone service.
